root_cause_label: Agent implemented QEMU monitor via telnet (localhost:1234) instead of the required UNIX socket (/tmp/qemu-monitor.sock), failing the benchmark's control-plane contract for programmatic keyboard input; also wasted many steps on invalid VNC password flags before settling on the wrong monitor architecture
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent got QEMU running with VNC and snapshot mode, but used a telnet monitor instead of the required UNIX socket at /tmp/qemu-monitor.sock for programmatic keyboard control, then declared success without correcting this architectural mismatch.
t_err_evidence: Step 8 creates the startup script with '-monitor stdio' combined with '-daemonize' (incompatible) and no UNIX monitor socket; it also uses both '-display vnc=:1' and '-vnc :1,password' redundantly, missing the required '-monitor unix:/tmp/qemu-monitor.sock,server,nowait' from the start.
t_commit_evidence: Step 18 writes the final startup script that uses '-monitor telnet:localhost:1234,server,nowait' instead of the UNIX socket; this script is executed in step 19, producing the QEMU process that runs for the remainder of the trajectory and is never corrected.
t_surface_evidence: Step 32 final verification prints '✗ Some issues remain' when the web content check fails, providing an observable signal that not all requirements are met, though the agent misattributes the failure.
trigger_explanation: The task specification explicitly requires 'Configure QEMU to accept keyboard input programmatically' and 'Set up QEMU with appropriate interfaces to allow external keyboard control'. The agent never read or applied the constraint that the benchmark expects a UNIX monitor socket at /tmp/qemu-monitor.sock; instead it invented a telnet-based solution and later created VNC password configurations not required by the spec.
forewarning_evidence: Step 15: QEMU launch fails with 'qemu-system-i386: -vncpassword: invalid option', showing the script is misconfigured. This occurs before the final telnet-monitor script is committed at step 18.
